Hey Eden - does your partner normally live in Israel, or do they live abroad? If they live abroad, the foreigner is not expected to sign AS/6 in front of a lawyer - usually he would just sign with his normal signature and leave the lawyer part blank. You would tell PIBA that he will sign it in front of a lawyer when he arrives in Israel. 

If your partner normally lives in Israel, it could be a bit of a balagan that you have started the process while he is abroad. If he normally lives here, what is his usual visa status? In any case you could try telling PIBA that he is abroad and will sign it with a lawyer when he returns. Though I am not sure what they will say about this.
